claims.text: High configurational entropy in HEAs produces significant lattice distortion.
Lattice distortion activates and couples multiple dislocation and twinning mechanisms during high-strain-rate deformation.
Coupled dislocation and twinning mechanisms enhance dynamic strain hardening.
A random distribution of multiple principal elements creates a highly distorted lattice in an as-cast or homogenized HEA.
Multi-element solid-solution lattice distortion creates local variations in elastic modulus.
Multi-element solid-solution lattice distortion creates local variations in energy barriers for dislocation motion.
The heterogeneous local environment in HEAs hampers dislocation glide under dynamic loading.
Hindered dislocation glide promotes multiple deformation modes, including dislocation motion coupled with localized lattice rotation or twinning.
HEAs will have higher strain-rate sensitivity than a compositionally similar conventional low-configurational-entropy alloy.
HEAs will have greater dynamic strain hardening than the baseline conventional alloy.
HEAs will exhibit increased dynamic yield strength relative to the baseline conventional alloy.
HEAs will exhibit greater work hardening under dynamic loading than the baseline conventional alloy.
Evidence of multiple slip systems or twinning will be more pronounced in HEAs than in the baseline alloy after dynamic deformation.
Temperatures below approximately half the melting temperature ensure dislocation-dominated plasticity during the proposed tests.
The hypothesis applies to HEAs having at least five principal elements in near-equal proportions and substantial lattice distortion.
The proposed mechanism may cease to apply at very high temperatures where thermal activation dominates.
Excessive annealing can reduce lattice distortion and thereby place an HEA outside the proposed mechanism's domain.
